title: Perimeter of Polygons and Missing Side Lengths
seo_title: Grade 3 Perimeter Worksheets: Missing Side Lengths (TEKS 3.7B, STAAR)
standard_text: 3.7B determine the perimeter of a polygon or a missing length when given perimeter and remaining side lengths in problems
meta_desc: Free Grade 3 perimeter worksheets for Texas TEKS 3.7B: add side lengths, count units around, rectangles and squares, missing side lengths and perimeter and area word problems. 100 STAAR-style questions with answers.
key_big: Perimeter is the distance around: add all the sides.
key_sub: For a missing side, add the known sides and subtract from the perimeter.
body_html:
How to think about it

  • Perimeter is the distance around a shape. Add the lengths of all the sides.
  • A rectangle has 2 pairs of equal sides: perimeter = length + width + length + width. A square has 4 equal sides.
  • To find a missing side, add the sides you know and subtract from the perimeter.
  • Perimeter is measured in units (cm, in., ft). Area is measured in square units.

Examples

Example

A rectangle is 8 ft long and 5 ft wide. What is its perimeter?

8 + 5 + 8 + 5

= 26

Answer: 26 ft

Example

A triangle has a perimeter of 30 cm. Two sides are 9 cm and 12 cm. How long is the third side?

9 + 12 = 21

30 − 21 = 9

Answer: 9 cm

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Adding only the labeled sides of a rectangleOpposite sides are equal. Add all 4 sides.
Multiplying length × widthThat is area. Perimeter adds the sides.
Counting the squares inside the shapeCount the unit edges around the outside.

faq.a: Find the perimeter of a polygon, or a missing side length when the perimeter and the other side lengths are given, in problems.

faq.q: How do you find the perimeter of a rectangle?
faq.a: Add all four sides: length + width + length + width. For 7 by 3, that is 7 + 3 + 7 + 3 = 20.

faq.q: How do you find a missing side?
faq.a: Add the known sides, then subtract that sum from the perimeter.

faq.q: What is the difference between perimeter and area?
faq.a: Perimeter is the distance around (units). Area is the space inside (square units).

items.q: Jack wants to put a fence around a garden that is 9 meters long and 6 meters wide. How many meters of fence are needed?
items.e: The fence goes all the way around: 9 + 6 + 9 + 6 = 30 m.

items.q: Ava glues ribbon around the edge of a square picture frame. Each side is 8 inches. How much ribbon is needed?
items.e: 4 equal sides: 4 × 8 = 32 inches.

items.q: A park is shaped like a triangle. Its sides are 120 m, 150 m and 90 m. Leo walks once around the park. How far does he walk?
items.e: Add the 3 sides: 120 + 150 + 90 = 360 m.

items.q: A rug is 7 feet long and 5 feet wide. Trim is sewn around all of its edges. How many feet of trim are used?
items.e: Perimeter = 7 + 5 + 7 + 5 = 24 ft. (35 sq ft would be the area of the rug.)

items.q: A rabbit pen is 10 feet long and 4 feet wide. One long side is against a wall, so it needs no fence. How many feet of fence are needed for the other 3 sides?
items.e: Only 3 sides get fence: 10 + 4 + 4 = 18 ft.

items.q: Noah used 30 feet of fence to go around a rectangular dog run. The dog run is 9 feet long. How wide is it?
items.e: Two lengths: 9 + 9 = 18. 30 − 18 = 12 for two widths. 12 ÷ 2 = 6 ft.

items.q: A square playground has sides of 25 meters. A coach runs around it 2 times. How far does the coach run?
items.e: Once around is 4 × 25 = 100 m. Two times around is 100 + 100 = 200 m.

items.q: A sign has 5 sides: 6, 6, 4, 4, 5 inches. What is the perimeter of the sign?
items.e: Add all 5 sides: 6 + 6 + 4 + 4 + 5 = 25 inches.

items.q: A classroom table is 30 inches long and 20 inches wide. Lily puts tape around the top edge. A roll has 120 inches of tape. Is one roll enough?
items.e: Perimeter = 30 + 20 + 30 + 20 = 100 inches. 100 is less than 120, so one roll is enough. (600 is the area. 50 is only one length and one width.)

items.q: A garden shaped like a hexagon has 6 equal sides. The fence around it is 24 meters long. How long is each side?
items.e: 6 equal sides share the 24 meters: 24 ÷ 6 = 4 m.

items.q: Each rectangle is measured in units. Which rectangle has a perimeter of 20 units?
items.e: 2 + 8 + 2 + 8 = 20. A quick way: length + width must be half of 20, which is 10.

items.q: Each rectangle is measured in units. Which rectangle has a perimeter of 24 units?
items.e: 3 + 9 + 3 + 9 = 24. A quick way: length + width must be half of 24, which is 12.

items.q: Each rectangle is measured in units. Which rectangle has a perimeter of 16 units?
items.e: 2 + 6 + 2 + 6 = 16. A quick way: length + width must be half of 16, which is 8.

items.q: Each rectangle is measured in units. Which rectangle has a perimeter of 28 units?
items.e: 3 + 11 + 3 + 11 = 28. A quick way: length + width must be half of 28, which is 14.

items.q: Each rectangle is measured in units. Which rectangle has a perimeter of 18 units?
items.e: 3 + 6 + 3 + 6 = 18. A quick way: length + width must be half of 18, which is 9.

items.q: Rectangle A is 2 by 8 units. Rectangle B is 4 by 4 units. Both have an area of 16 square units. Which has the greater perimeter?
items.e: A: 2 + 8 + 2 + 8 = 20 units. B: 4 + 4 + 4 + 4 = 16 units. Same area does not mean same perimeter. The long, thin rectangle has more edge.

items.q: Rectangle A is 3 by 8 units. Rectangle B is 4 by 6 units. Both have an area of 24 square units. Which has the greater perimeter?
items.e: A: 3 + 8 + 3 + 8 = 22 units. B: 4 + 6 + 4 + 6 = 20 units. Same area does not mean same perimeter. The long, thin rectangle has more edge.

items.q: Rectangle A is 1 by 12 units. Rectangle B is 3 by 4 units. Both have an area of 12 square units. Which has the greater perimeter?
items.e: A: 1 + 12 + 1 + 12 = 26 units. B: 3 + 4 + 3 + 4 = 14 units. Same area does not mean same perimeter. The long, thin rectangle has more edge.

items.q: Rectangle A is 3 by 7 units. Rectangle B is 5 by 5 units. Both have a perimeter of 20 units. Which has the greater area?
items.e: A: 3 × 7 = 21 square units. B: 5 × 5 = 25 square units. Same perimeter does not mean same area. The shape closer to a square holds more space.

items.q: Rectangle A is 2 by 8 units. Rectangle B is 4 by 6 units. Both have a perimeter of 20 units. Which has the greater area?
items.e: A: 2 × 8 = 16 square units. B: 4 × 6 = 24 square units. Same perimeter does not mean same area. The shape closer to a square holds more space.
